messages:
Anya (Docs): Quick sync — I'm drafting a new subsection for the Regions & Residency page about Private / on-prem deployments. Need a short SDK snippet + curl example showing how to indicate region/residency when calling a private control plane.
Sam (Platform): For Private we usually rely on the X-Redwood-Region header + the account's residency flag. Can you show both?
Anya (Docs): Yup — plan is to show: header + query param fallback + note about KMS locality. Also we should fix two broken anchors on the page (the on-prem heading moved). PR will include link fixes.
Luis (Eng): Here's a minimal curl example we use internally:
```bash
curl -sS 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  https://private-controlplane.company.internal/v1/generate 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-instruct-4x","input":"hello"}'
```
Luis (Eng): For SDKs recommend setting `region` on the client config (Node/python) so it flows to all requests. Also mention that the platform will override if account residency is set to a different region.
Anya (Docs): Perfect — can you paste short Node + Python snippets I can drop in? Keep them under 6 lines each.
Luis (Eng): Node:```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, region: 'eu' });
const res = await client.responses.create({ model: 'redwood-instruct-4x', input: 'hi' });
console.log(res.output[0].content[0].text);
```
Luis (Eng): Python:```py
from redwood import Redwood
client = Redwood(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'), region='eu')
print(client.responses.create(model='redwood-instruct-4x', input='hi'))
```
Sam (Platform): One caveat: for air-gapped on-prem installs the control-plane URL will differ; add a short note: "replace control plane host with your deployment URL".
Anya (Docs): Adding that. Also want to add a small callout: "If your org has EU residency enforced, setting header won't bypass policy — contact SRE for exceptions."
Maya (Legal): +1 on the callout. Also add a link to the data residency compliance FAQ and the Customer DPA paragraph. 
Anya (Docs): Will link to /docs/compliance/data-residency and to the DPA snippet. Some anchors changed after last restructure — two links currently 404. I'll update them in the PR.
docs-ci-bot: docs lint check started for PR #4821 - redwood/docs — running link-checker.
Anya (Docs): PR is here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4821 — includes: new on-prem residency snippet, Node/Python examples, anchor fixes, and small legal callout.
Sam (Platform): :eyes: I'll review for accuracy (headers + param names).
Luis (Eng): Minor suggestion: use `eu` as residency token in examples (not `eu-west-1`) to match control-plane canonical values.
Anya (Docs): Good catch. Updated snippets.
Maya (Legal): Approved copy for the legal callout.
docs-ci-bot: link-checker found 2 broken anchors: /docs/compliance#data-residency (line 42) and /docs/on-prem#deploy (line 89).
Anya (Docs): I'll patch those anchors in the same PR.
Sam (Platform): If you want, I can push a tiny change to the internal config to support the `region` param mapping for older SDKs. Will coordinate in the PR.
Anya (Docs): That would be great — please add a short note in the PR description about backward compatibility mapping.
docs-ci-bot: docs lint passed, link-checker re-run OK.
Anya (Docs): Merged to staging. Thanks everyone. :tada:
Sam (Platform): :+1: Will follow up if any runtime detail needs tightening.
Luis (Eng): Thanks — will open a tech note if anything changes for air-gapped installs.
Maya (Legal): Thanks all.
Anya (Docs): Closing — will cherry-pick to main after enterprise review.
